$d i_x \alpha = 0$, and $i_x^*\alpha$ represents the class $[\bar \alpha] \in H^1(\mathbb{R}P^1)$.
$d\alpha = \frac{1}{2} \pi^*(\Omega)$.

nodes.name: Index formula for sections of a projective bundle
nodes.statement: Let $E \to M$ be a vector bundle and $Q = P(E)$. Assume that $g$ is a metric in $E$. Let $\Omega$ be the curvature form of the connection in $Q$ induced by a connection in $E$ adapted to $g$. Let $a \in H^1(\mathbb{R}P^1)$ is represented by the form $\bar \alpha$. If $s : M \setminus \Sigma \to Q$ is a section with singularities, \begin{equation} ind (s; a) = \int_M \Omega. \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: For a singular section of $Q=P(E)$ the total index equals $\int_M\Omega$.
assumptions: Let $E \to M$ be a vector bundle and $Q = P(E)$.
Assume that $g$ is a metric in $E$.
Let $\Omega$ be the curvature form of the connection in $Q$ induced by a connection in $E$ adapted to $g$.
Let $a \in H^1(\mathbb{R}P^1)$ is represented by the form $\bar \alpha$.
If $s : M \setminus \Sigma \to Q$ is a section with singularities,
conclusions: ind (s; a) = \int_M \Omega.

nodes.name: principal $G$-bundle with singularities $\Sigma$
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{G}$ be a Lie group, and $G\subset \bar{G}$ be a Lie subgroup of $G$. Let $M$ be a manifold, and $\Sigma$ be a submanifold of $M$. A principal $\bar{G}$-bundle $\bar{P}(M, \bar{G})$ is called a \emph{principal $G$-bundle with singularities $\Sigma$} if the structure group $\bar{G}$ of $\bar{P}|_{M\setminus \Sigma}$ reduces to $G$.
nodes.statement_short: A $\bar G$-bundle whose structure group reduces to $G$ only off a submanifold $\Sigma$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
differentia: the structure group $\bar{G}$ of $\bar{P}|_{M\setminus \Sigma}$ reduces to $G$

nodes.name: Frame bundle as a $GL(n-1)$-bundle with singularities
nodes.statement: Let $X$ be a vector field on a manifold $M$ with a discrete set of zeros $\Sigma \subset M$. Then the frame bundle $L(M)$ is a principal $GL(n-1)$-bundle with singularities on $M$. It is clear that on $M \setminus \Sigma$ the bundle $L(M)$ reduces to the principal $GL(n-1)$-subbundle consisting of frames with the first vector equal to the value of $X$ at the corresponding point.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Orthonormal frame bundle as an $\{e\}$-bundle with singularities
nodes.statement: If $M$ is a two-dimensional oriented Riemannian manifold, and $X$ is a vector field on $M$ with a discrete set of zeros $\Sigma \subset M$, then the orthonormal frame bundle $SO(M)$ is a principal $\{e\}$-bundle with singularities where the set of singularities $\Sigma$ because the vector field induced trivialization of $SO(M)$ over $M \setminus \Sigma$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Frame bundle with empty singular set
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a Riemannian manifold of dimension $n$. The principal $GL(n)$-bundle of frames $L(M)$ is a principal $O(n)$-bundle with an empty set of singularities.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Reductions of a principal bundle correspond to sections of $P/H$
nodes.statement: Let $P$ be a $G$-principal bundle and let $H$ be a Lie subgroup of $G$. Then $G$ has a reduction to a principal $H$-bundle if and only if the associated bundle $P/H\rightarrow M$ admits a section.In particular, if $H=\{e\}$ then $P$ has a section.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: Let $P$ be a $G$-principal bundle and let $H$ be a Lie subgroup of $G$.
conclusions: Then $G$ has a reduction to a principal $H$-bundle if and only if the associated bundle $P/H\rightarrow M$ admits a section.In particular, if $H=\{e\}$ then $P$ has a section.

nodes.name: A $G$-bundle with singularities yields a singular section of $\bar{P}/G$
nodes.statement: Let $\bar{P}(M, \bar{G}, \pi)$ a principal $G$-bundle with singularities, and let $\Sigma$ be the set of singularities. Then there is a section $s: M\setminus \Sigma \rightarrow \bar{P}/G$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: Let $\bar{P}(M, \bar{G}, \pi)$ a principal $G$-bundle with singularities, and let $\Sigma$ be the set of singularities.
conclusions: Then there is a section $s: M\setminus \Sigma \rightarrow \bar{P}/G$.

nodes.name: $\widetilde{\omega}$ is an equivariant projector onto $\bar{V}$
nodes.statement: a) $\widetilde{\omega}$ is a field of projectors onto the vertical distribution $\bar{V}$ with kernel $\bar{H}$. b) $\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}} \circ dR_{\bar{g}} (\bar{X}) = dR_{\bar{g}} \circ \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}} (\bar{X})$, where $R_{\bar{g}} : \bar{G} \to \bar{G}$, $R_{\bar{g}} \bar{g}' = \bar{g}' \bar{g}$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: Assume that $\bar{P}$ is endowed with a connection form $\bar{\omega}: T\bar{P} \rightarrow \bar{\mathfrak{g}}$, and let $\bar{H} = \ker\bar{\omega}$ be the horizontal distribution of the connection, and $\bar{V}=\ker d\pi$ the vertical distribution on $\bar{P}$.
conclusions: a) $\widetilde{\omega}$ is a field of projectors onto the vertical distribution $\bar{V}$ with kernel $\bar{H}$.

b) $\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}} \circ dR_{\bar{g}} (\bar{X}) = dR_{\bar{g}} \circ \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}} (\bar{X})$, where $R_{\bar{g}} : \bar{G} \to \bar{G}$, $R_{\bar{g}} \bar{g}' = \bar{g}' \bar{g}$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\widetilde{\omega}$ is an equivariant projector
nodes.statement: It is clear that $\widetilde{\omega}$ vanishes on $\bar{H}$. For $\bar{X} \in \bar{V}_{\bar{p}}$, $\bar{p} \in \bar{P}$, one can find $\bar{a} \in \bar{\mathfrak{g}}$ such that $\sigma_{\bar{p}}(\bar{a}) = \bar{X}$. Then, $\bar{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X}) = \bar{a}$, hence follows that $\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X}) = \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) = X$. Thus we get a). Now a) implies b) because $dR_{\bar{g}} : T_{\bar{p}} \bar{P} \to T_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}\bar{P}$ is an isomorphism, which maps $\bar{H}_{\bar{p}}$ to $\bar{H}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}$, and $\bar{V}_{\bar{p}}$ to $\bar{V}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}$.
nodes.statement_short: Check $\widetilde\omega$ kills $\bar H$ and is the identity on $\bar V$; equivariance then follows since $dR_{\bar g}$ preserves the splitting.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Item a): projector property
nodes.statement: It is clear that $\widetilde{\omega}$ vanishes on $\bar{H}$. For $\bar{X} \in \bar{V}_{\bar{p}}$, $\bar{p} \in \bar{P}$, one can find $\bar{a} \in \bar{\mathfrak{g}}$ such that $\sigma_{\bar{p}}(\bar{a}) = \bar{X}$. Then, $\bar{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X}) = \bar{a}$, hence follows that $\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X}) = \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) = X$. Thus we get a).
nodes.statement_short: Fundamental vector fields realize every vertical vector, so $\widetilde\omega$ acts as the identity on $\bar V$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Item b): equivariance
nodes.statement: Now a) implies b) because $dR_{\bar{g}} : T_{\bar{p}} \bar{P} \to T_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}\bar{P}$ is an isomorphism, which maps $\bar{H}_{\bar{p}}$ to $\bar{H}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}$, and $\bar{V}_{\bar{p}}$ to $\bar{V}_{\bar{p}\bar{g}}$.
nodes.statement_short: $dR_{\bar g}$ preserves the horizontal-vertical splitting, giving equivariance.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Projection of the connection to $E = \bar{P}/G$
nodes.statement: a) There exists a operator field $\omega_E$ on $E$ such that, for each $\bar{p} \in \bar{P}$, the following diagram is commutative: \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ T_{\bar{p}} \bar{P} \ar[r]^{\widetilde{\omega}} \ar[d]_{d\pi_G} & \bar{V}_{\bar{p}} \ar[d]^{d\pi_G} \\ T_{\pi_G(p)} E \ar[r]^{\omega_E} & VE_{\pi_G(p)} } \end{equation} b) $\omega_E$ is a projector onto $VE$ with kernel $HE = \ker\omega_E = d\pi_G(\bar{H})$. c) The decomposition $T\bar{P}= \bar{H} \oplus \bar{V}$ of $T\bar{P}$ projects onto a decomposition $TE=HE\oplus VE$ of $TE$ via $d\pi_G$.
nodes.statement_short: The projector $\widetilde\omega$ descends through $d\pi_G$ to a projector $\omega_E$ on $TE$, giving the induced splitting $TE = HE \oplus VE$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: Assume that $\bar{P}$ is endowed with a connection form $\bar{\omega}: T\bar{P} \rightarrow \bar{\mathfrak{g}}$, and let $\bar{H} = \ker\bar{\omega}$ be the horizontal distribution of the connection, and $\bar{V}=\ker d\pi$ the vertical distribution on $\bar{P}$.
conclusions: a) There exists a operator field $\omega_E$ on $E$ such that, for each $\bar{p} \in \bar{P}$, the following diagram is commutative:
b) $\omega_E$ is a projector onto $VE$ with kernel $HE = \ker\omega_E = d\pi_G(\bar{H})$.
c) The decomposition $T\bar{P}= \bar{H} \oplus \bar{V}$ of $T\bar{P}$ projects onto a decomposition $TE=HE\oplus VE$ of $TE$ via $d\pi_G$.

nodes.name: Proof that $\omega_E$ is well defined and projects the splitting
nodes.statement: a) If $d\pi_G(\bar{X}_{\bar{p}}) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}'_{\bar{p'}})$, then $\bar{p}' = \bar{p} g$, and $\bar{X}' = dR_g \bar{X} + \bar{Y}$, where $g \in G$ and $\bar{Y} = \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a) \in \ker d\pi_G$ with $a \in \mathfrak{g}$. By Lemma~\ref{lm:3}, we have \begin{equation} \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(\bar{X}') =\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(dR_g \bar{X} + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a)) = \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(dR_g \bar{X}) + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a) = dR_g (\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(X) + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a). \end{equation} Then, \begin{equation} d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X})) = d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}'}(\bar{X}')), \end{equation} this proves that $\omega_E$ in the diagram~\eqref{eq:76} is well defined. b) From the diagram~\eqref{eq:76} it follows that $d\pi_G(\bar{H}) \subset HE$. For any $X \in HE_{\pi_G(\bar{p})}$, take $\bar{X} \in T_{\pi_G(\bar{p})} \bar{P}$ such that $d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$. Then $d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X})) = 0$, this means that $\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X}) = \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a)$, where $a \in \mathfrak{g}$. Then $\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a)) = 0$, therefore $\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) \in \bar{H}_{\bar{p}}$ and $d\pi_G(\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) \in \bar{H}_{\bar{p}}) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$. Thus $HE \subset d\pi_G(\bar{H})$ and therefore $HE = d\pi_G(\bar{H})$. For any $X \in VE_{\pi_G(\bar{p})}$, $X = d\pi_G(\bar{X})$, where $\bar{X} \in \bar{V}$. Then, by Lemma~\ref{lm:3} and \eqref{eq:76}, we have that $\omega_E(X) = d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X})) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$. c) follows from b).
nodes.statement_short: Well-definedness from the equivariance in Lemma 3, then a two-inclusion argument for $HE = d\pi_G(\bar H)$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Item a): $\omega_E$ is well defined
nodes.statement: a) If $d\pi_G(\bar{X}_{\bar{p}}) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}'_{\bar{p'}})$, then $\bar{p}' = \bar{p} g$, and $\bar{X}' = dR_g \bar{X} + \bar{Y}$, where $g \in G$ and $\bar{Y} = \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a) \in \ker d\pi_G$ with $a \in \mathfrak{g}$. By Lemma~\ref{lm:3}, we have \begin{equation} \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(\bar{X}') =\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(dR_g \bar{X} + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a)) = \widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p} g}(dR_g \bar{X}) + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a) = dR_g (\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(X) + \sigma_{\bar{p} g}(a). \end{equation} Then, \begin{equation} d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}}(\bar{X})) = d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}_{\bar{p}'}(\bar{X}')), \end{equation} this proves that $\omega_E$ in the diagram~\eqref{eq:76} is well defined.
nodes.statement_short: Two lifts of the same tangent vector differ by an equivariant term killed by $d\pi_G$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Item b): identification of $HE$ and $VE$
nodes.statement: b) From the diagram~\eqref{eq:76} it follows that $d\pi_G(\bar{H}) \subset HE$. For any $X \in HE_{\pi_G(\bar{p})}$, take $\bar{X} \in T_{\pi_G(\bar{p})} \bar{P}$ such that $d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$. Then $d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X})) = 0$, this means that $\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X}) = \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a)$, where $a \in \mathfrak{g}$. Then $\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a)) = 0$, therefore $\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) \in \bar{H}_{\bar{p}}$ and $d\pi_G(\bar{X}) - \sigma_{\bar{p}}(a) \in \bar{H}_{\bar{p}}) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$. Thus $HE \subset d\pi_G(\bar{H})$ and therefore $HE = d\pi_G(\bar{H})$. For any $X \in VE_{\pi_G(\bar{p})}$, $X = d\pi_G(\bar{X})$, where $\bar{X} \in \bar{V}$. Then, by Lemma~\ref{lm:3} and \eqref{eq:76}, we have that $\omega_E(X) = d\pi_G(\widetilde{\omega}(\bar{X})) = d\pi_G(\bar{X}) = X$.
nodes.statement_short: Double inclusion gives $HE=d\pi_G(\bar H)$, and $\omega_E$ is the identity on $VE$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Item c): the splitting descends
nodes.statement: c) follows from b).
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: $E$ as the associated bundle with fibre $\bar{G}/G$
nodes.statement: The bundle $E \to M$ is the bundle associated with the principal $\bar{G}$-bundle $\bar{P} \to M$ with the fiber $\bar{G}/G$ with respect to the left action of $\bar{G}$ on $\bar{G}/G$. The distribution $HE$ is the connection induced on the associated bundle by the connection $\bar{H}$ on $\bar{P}$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: The vertical bundle $VE$ as an associated bundle with fibre $\mathfrak{m}$
nodes.statement: The vertical subbundle $VE$ is isomorphic to the bundle associated with the principal $G$-bundle $\pi_G : \bar{P} \to E$ with the fiber $\mathfrak{m}$ with respect to the left action of $G$ on $\mathfrak{m}$: $L_g (a) = ad(g^{-1}) a$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: As $\bar{G}$ is compact, the homogeneous space $\bar{G}/G$ is reductive, this means that we have $ad(G)$-invariant decomposition $\bar{\mathfrak{g}} = \mathfrak{g} \oplus \mathfrak{m}$.
conclusions: The vertical subbundle $VE$ is isomorphic to the bundle associated with the principal $G$-bundle $\pi_G : \bar{P} \to E$ with the fiber $\mathfrak{m}$ with respect to the left action of $G$ on $\mathfrak{m}$: $L_g (a) = ad(g^{-1}) a$.

nodes.name: Proof of the identification of $VE$
nodes.statement: The isomorphism $V_E \cong \bar{P}\times_{\bar{G}} \bar{G} \times \bar{\mathfrak{g}}/\mathfrak{g} \cong \bar{P}\times_G \mathfrak{m}$ follows from the fact that $VE=\bar{P}\times_{\bar{G}} T(\bar{G}/G)$~\cite{michor2000}(Chapter IV, section 18.18) and that $T(\bar{G}/G)=\bar{G}\times \bar {\mathfrak{g}} / \mathfrak{g}$~\cite{sharpe2000}(Chapter 4, section 5). In the exact form the isomorphism is written as follows: \begin{equation} \bar{P}\times_G \mathfrak{m} \to VE, \quad [\bar{p}, a] \mapsto d\pi_G(\sigma_{\bar{p}} (a)). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Chain the standard identifications $VE=\bar P\times_{\bar G}T(\bar G/G)$ and $T(\bar G/G)=\bar G\times\bar{\mathfrak g}/\mathfrak g$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Chain the standard identifications
nodes.statement: The isomorphism $V_E \cong \bar{P}\times_{\bar{G}} \bar{G} \times \bar{\mathfrak{g}}/\mathfrak{g} \cong \bar{P}\times_G \mathfrak{m}$ follows from the fact that $VE=\bar{P}\times_{\bar{G}} T(\bar{G}/G)$~\cite{michor2000}(Chapter IV, section 18.18) and that $T(\bar{G}/G)=\bar{G}\times \bar {\mathfrak{g}} / \mathfrak{g}$~\cite{sharpe2000}(Chapter 4, section 5).
nodes.statement_short: Compose the known descriptions of $VE$ and of $T(\bar G/G)$ to get $\bar P\times_G\mathfrak m$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Write the isomorphism explicitly
nodes.statement: In the exact form the isomorphism is written as follows: \begin{equation} \bar{P}\times_G \mathfrak{m} \to VE, \quad [\bar{p}, a] \mapsto d\pi_G(\sigma_{\bar{p}} (a)). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Give the explicit map $[\bar p,a]\mapsto d\pi_G(\sigma_{\bar p}(a))$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Explicit vertical form on $E = \bar{P}/G$
nodes.statement: Let $\omega_E: TE \rightarrow VE$ be a connection form induced by a connection in the principal $\bar{G}$-bundle $\bar{P} \to M$ (see~Statement~\ref{stat:11}). Then \begin{equation} \alpha(X)=\tilde{\alpha}(\omega_E(X)) \end{equation} The form $\alpha$ given by~\eqref{eq:81} satisfies the properties (1) and (2) of Statement~\ref{stat:1}.
nodes.statement_short: For a homogeneous fibre, $\alpha=\tilde\alpha\circ\omega_E$ built from an invariant form gives the vertical form of Statement 1 explicitly.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities
assumptions: Let $\omega_E: TE \rightarrow VE$ be a connection form induced by a connection in the principal $\bar{G}$-bundle $\bar{P} \to M$ (see~Statement~\ref{stat:11}).
conclusions: \alpha(X)=\tilde{\alpha}(\omega_E(X))
The form $\alpha$ given by~\eqref{eq:81} satisfies the properties (1) and (2) of Statement~\ref{stat:1}.

nodes.name: Proof that $\alpha = \tilde{\alpha}\circ\omega_E$ has properties (1) and (2)
nodes.statement: For $X \in H$, $\omega_E(X) = 0$, therefore $\alpha(X) = 0$. Recall that the trivializations of $E = P/G$ are constructed in the following way. For a good covering $U_i$ of $M$ we take sections $s_i : U_i \to P$, then we define the charts \begin{equation} \psi_i : U_i \times \bar{G}/G \to \pi_E^{-1}(U_i), \quad (x, [\bar{g}]) \to [s_i(x) \bar{g}] = \pi_G(s_i(x) \bar{g}). \end{equation} Therefore, for $x \in U_i$, $\eta_x^{-1} : \bar{G}/G \to E_x = \pi_E^{-1}(x)$, $\eta_x^{-1}[\bar{g}] = \pi_G(s_i(x)\bar{g})$. Now let us fix $x \in U_i \subset M$ and let $\bar{p} = s_i(x)$. For any $y \in E_x$ and $Y \in V_yE$, we have that $y = \pi_G(\bar{p} \bar{g}) = [\bar{p}, \bar{g}] = \eta_x^{-1}(\bar{g})$ and $Y = d\pi_G(\sigma_{\bar{p} \bar{g}}(a)) = [\bar{p} \bar{g}, a] = d\eta_x^{-1} (dL_{\bar{g}} a)$, where $a \in \mathfrak{m}$, and $L_{\bar{g}} : \bar{G}/G \to \bar{G}/G$, $L_{\bar{g}} \bar{g}' = \bar{g}\bar{g}'$. Note that here we use the isomorphism constructed in Lemma~\ref{lm:4}. Then \begin{equation} \alpha(Y) = \widetilde{\alpha}(\omega_E(Y)) = \widetilde{\alpha}(Y) = \xi_0(a) = \xi(dL_{\bar{g}} a). \end{equation} Therefore $\alpha(d\eta_x^{-1} (dL_{\bar{g}} a) ) = \xi(dL_{\bar{g}} a)$, thus $(\eta_x^{-1})^* \left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} = \xi$, then $\eta_x^* \xi = \left.\alpha\right|_{E_x}$. Thus $d\left(\left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} \right) = 0$, and $\left[\left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} \right] = H^1(\eta_x) a$.
nodes.statement_short: Property (1) is immediate; property (2) follows by computing $\alpha$ on vertical vectors in the standard trivializations of $\bar P/G$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Property (1): $\alpha$ vanishes on $H$
nodes.statement: For $X \in H$, $\omega_E(X) = 0$, therefore $\alpha(X) = 0$.
nodes.statement_short: Property (1) is immediate.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Recall the trivializations of $E = P/G$
nodes.statement: Recall that the trivializations of $E = P/G$ are constructed in the following way. For a good covering $U_i$ of $M$ we take sections $s_i : U_i \to P$, then we define the charts \begin{equation} \psi_i : U_i \times \bar{G}/G \to \pi_E^{-1}(U_i), \quad (x, [\bar{g}]) \to [s_i(x) \bar{g}] = \pi_G(s_i(x) \bar{g}). \end{equation} Therefore, for $x \in U_i$, $\eta_x^{-1} : \bar{G}/G \to E_x = \pi_E^{-1}(x)$, $\eta_x^{-1}[\bar{g}] = \pi_G(s_i(x)\bar{g})$.
nodes.statement_short: Set up the charts $\psi_i$ and the fibre identifications $\eta_x$.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Compute $\alpha$ on vertical vectors
nodes.statement: Now let us fix $x \in U_i \subset M$ and let $\bar{p} = s_i(x)$. For any $y \in E_x$ and $Y \in V_yE$, we have that $y = \pi_G(\bar{p} \bar{g}) = [\bar{p}, \bar{g}] = \eta_x^{-1}(\bar{g})$ and $Y = d\pi_G(\sigma_{\bar{p} \bar{g}}(a)) = [\bar{p} \bar{g}, a] = d\eta_x^{-1} (dL_{\bar{g}} a)$, where $a \in \mathfrak{m}$, and $L_{\bar{g}} : \bar{G}/G \to \bar{G}/G$, $L_{\bar{g}} \bar{g}' = \bar{g}\bar{g}'$. Note that here we use the isomorphism constructed in Lemma~\ref{lm:4}. Then \begin{equation} \alpha(Y) = \widetilde{\alpha}(\omega_E(Y)) = \widetilde{\alpha}(Y) = \xi_0(a) = \xi(dL_{\bar{g}} a). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Using the isomorphism of Lemma 4, $\alpha(Y)=\xi(dL_{\bar g}a)$ on vertical vectors.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Property (2): conclude $\eta_x^*\xi = \alpha|_{E_x}$
nodes.statement: Therefore $\alpha(d\eta_x^{-1} (dL_{\bar{g}} a) ) = \xi(dL_{\bar{g}} a)$, thus $(\eta_x^{-1})^* \left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} = \xi$, then $\eta_x^* \xi = \left.\alpha\right|_{E_x}$. Thus $d\left(\left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} \right) = 0$, and $\left[\left.\alpha\right|_{E_x} \right] = H^1(\eta_x) a$.
nodes.statement_short: Invariance of $\xi$ gives closedness of the fibre restriction and the right cohomology class.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Curvature via the Frölicher-Nijenhuis bracket
nodes.statement: The curvature form $\Omega_E= D\omega_E$ of the connection $\omega_E$ (see Section~\ref{sec:3}, equation~\eqref{eq:25}) can be represented by the following equality: \begin{equation} \Omega_E=1/2[\omega_E, \omega_E], \end{equation} where $[ \ , \ ]: \Omega^{k}(E, TE)\times \Omega^{l}(E, TE)\rightarrow \Omega^{k+l}(E, TE)$ is the Frolicher-Nijenhuis bracket~\cite{michor2000}(Chapter IV, section 16.3).
nodes.statement_short: The curvature of the induced connection is $\tfrac12[\omega_E,\omega_E]$ for the Frölicher-Nijenhuis bracket.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: Bidegree splitting of $d\alpha$ in the principal bundle setting
nodes.statement: We repeat the arguments of subsection~\ref{subsec:3_4} and get that \begin{equation} d\alpha=L_X\alpha+1/2\tilde{\alpha}([\omega_E, \omega_E]). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Repeating the Section 3 computation gives $d\alpha=L_X\alpha+\tfrac12\tilde\alpha([\omega_E,\omega_E])$.

nodes.name: Hopf-Gauss-Bonnet theorem for principal $G$-bundle with singularities
nodes.statement: Thus, by assuming the existence of the $2$-dimensional oriented compact manifold $S$ and the map $q:S\rightarrow E$ satisfying the properties given in Section~\ref{sec:1}, by Theorem~\ref{thm:2}, we obtain the following equality \begin{equation} \int_S(q^{*}L_X\alpha +\frac{1}{2}q^{*}\tilde{\alpha}([\omega_E, \omega_E]))=\sum_{i=\overline{1, k}} index_{x_i}(s,a), \end{equation} where $s:M\setminus\Sigma \rightarrow E$ is the section corresponding to the reduction of $\bar{P}|_{M\setminus \Sigma}$ to $G$. The result given by the equation~\eqref{eq:86} will be called \emph{the Hopf-Gauss-Bonnet theorem for principal $G$-bundle with singularities}.
nodes.statement_short: For a $G$-bundle with singularities, the integral over $S$ of the connection/curvature terms equals the total index of the associated section.

assumptions: by assuming the existence of the $2$-dimensional oriented compact manifold $S$ and the map $q:S\rightarrow E$ satisfying the properties given in Section~\ref{sec:1}
conclusions: \int_S(q^{*}L_X\alpha +\frac{1}{2}q^{*}\tilde{\alpha}([\omega_E, \omega_E]))=\sum_{i=\overline{1, k}} index_{x_i}(s,a),

nodes.name: Recovering the classical Gauss-Bonnet theorem
nodes.statement: If $X$ is a vector field on $M$, and $\Sigma$ is the set of zeros of $X$, then $Y=\frac{X}{|X|}$ defines a section of the unit tangent bundle $M\rightarrow T^{1}M$ over $M\setminus \Sigma$. Since $T^{1}M$ is the associated bundle to the bundle of orthonormal frames $M\rightarrow SO(M)$ with respect of standard action of $SO(2)$ on $\mathbb{S}^{1}$, then $SO(M)|_{M\setminus \Sigma}$ reduces to the trivial subgroup $G=\{e \}$ of $\bar{G}=SO(2)$. Now, $\bar{G}/G=SO(2)$, and $SO(2)$ is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{S}^{1}$, then $H^{1}(\bar{G}/G)$ is $1$-dimensional vector space generated by the angle form on $\mathbb{S}^{1}$. Therefore, we can choose this generator to construct the form $\alpha\in \Omega^{1}(SO(M))$, and the connection form on $SO(M)$ induced by the Levi-Civita connection. This connection form is given by equation~\eqref{eq:42}. Thus, if $S$ and $q: S \rightarrow T^{1}M$ are the manifold and the map, respectively, constructed in section~\ref{sec:4}, the equation~\eqref{eq:86} reduces to the equation~\eqref{eq:46}. Hence, Hopf-Gauss-Bonnet theorem in principal $G$-bundle with singularities is a generalization of the classical Gauss-Bonnet theorem.
nodes.statement_short: Taking $\bar G=SO(2)$, $G=\{e\}$ reduces the general formula to the classical Gauss-Bonnet identity.
nodes.section: 5 Gauss-Bonnet Theorem in Principal $G$-bundles with Singularities

nodes.name: curvature of the connection $\omega_i$
nodes.statement: Let $dG_i = K_i \theta$, and call the function $K_i$ the \emph{curvature of the connection} $\omega_i$.

nodes.name: Hopf-Gauss-Bonnet theorem for a Whitney sum of rank-$2$ bundles
nodes.statement: Let $M$ be a compact connected two-dimensional manifold, let $E_i\rightarrow M, \ i=1, \cdots, k$, are $k$ vector bundles of rank $2$ over $M$, let $\tilde{E}_i =E_i\setminus s^0_i(M)$, where $s^0_i: M\rightarrow E_i$ is the zero section of $E_i$, and let $s_i : M \rightarrow E_i$ be a section of $E_i$ for each $i$. If $\omega_1, \cdots, \omega_k$ are connections on $E_1, \cdots, E_k$ respectively, $K_1, \cdots, K_k$ are the curvatures of these connections, and $s = (s_1, \cdots, s_k) : M\setminus \Sigma \rightarrow \tilde{E}$, then \begin{equation} \sum_{j=\overline{1, k}}\int_M K_i \theta = \sum_{x_i \in \Sigma} \sum_{j=\overline{1, k}}ind_{x_i}(s_j, [d\phi_j]), \end{equation} where $d\phi_i\in \Omega^{1}(\mathbb{R}^{2})$ is the angular form of $\mathbb{R}^{2}$, and $\theta$ is the area form on $M$.
nodes.statement_short: For $k$ rank-$2$ bundles the sum of total curvatures equals the sum over singular points of the indices of the component sections.

nodes.name: Proof of the Whitney-sum Hopf-Gauss-Bonnet theorem
nodes.statement: Let $S$ be an oriented $2$-manifold with boundary, and let $q: S \rightarrow E$ a map which satisfies the condition given in section~\ref{sec:1}, that is, $q_i$ restricted to $\overset{\circ}{S} = S \setminus \partial S$ is a diffeomorphism between $S \setminus \partial S$ and $s_i(M \setminus \Sigma)$. Now, because $E=\tilde{E}_1 \times \cdots \tilde{E}_k$, $q$ has the form $q=(q_1, \cdots, q_k)$, and for each $i$, the map $q_i: S\rightarrow \tilde{E}_i$ also satisfies this condition. This fact follows from the commutative diagram \begin{equation} \xymatrix{ & M\setminus \Sigma \ar[r]^{id} \ar[d]_{s} & M\setminus \Sigma \ar[d]^{s_i}\\ \overset{\circ}{S}\ar[r]^{q} & s(M\setminus \Sigma)\ar[r]^{\tilde{p}_i} & s_i(M\setminus \Sigma) } \end{equation} Since the vertical arrows are diffeomorphisms, we have that $q_i$ is a diffeomorphism. Therefore, for each $i = 1,\cdots, k$, the map $q_i=\tilde{p}_i\circ q$ is also a diffeomorphism. Let us take the cohomology class $a=[(d\phi_1, \cdots, d\phi_k)]$ of the fiber of $\tilde{E}$, where $d\phi_i$ is the angular form on the fiber $F_i$ of $E_i$, then $a=[d\phi_1]+ \cdots +[d\phi_k]$. Thus, the expression at the right side of equation~\eqref{eq:86} can be written as follows \begin{equation} \sum_{x_i \in \Sigma} index_{x_i}(s,a)=\sum_{x_i \in \Sigma} \sum_{j=\overline{1, k}}ind_{x_i}(s_j, [d\phi_j]). \end{equation} Furthermore, $d\overset{i}{G}=K_i \theta$, and $d\alpha =\sum_{j=\overline{1, k}} \pi^{*}(K_i \theta)$. Therefore, the expression at the left side of equation~\eqref{eq:86} reduces to the following equality \begin{equation} \int_S q^{*}\pi^{*}dG=\sum_{j=\overline{1, k}}\int_M K_i \theta \end{equation} Hence, we obtain the following equation \begin{equation} \sum_{i=\overline{1, k}}\int_M K_i \theta = \sum_{x_i \in \Sigma} \sum_{j=\overline{1, k}}ind_{x_i}(s_j, [d\phi_j]). \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Apply the general theorem to the product bundle: the components $q_i$ are diffeomorphisms, the index class splits as $\sum_j[d\phi_j]$, and the curvature term splits accordingly.
